messages:
Alice (infra): pagerduty alert - multiple private-subnet services in az-west-2b are seeing TCP resets to external APIs, spike in 5xxs and connection churn. alert group: VPC-EGRESS-RESET.
Ben (oncall): I'm on it. seeing large number of conn reset logs from NAT gateway nat-12345, conntrack shows entries flipping AZs.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-1764509876. Priority: P1. Paging oncall.
Ben (oncall): quick check - are these all from the same route table? running: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0aa*"`
Alice (infra): route table for private-subnet-a (subnet-0a1) was recently updated by terraform-apply at 16:12 UTC. It replaced a route pointing to nat-12345 with a route-prop to a new route-table association rt-0b2 (intent was for a different AZ).
Chris (prod-eng): customers reporting 504s from our webhook relay, correlation to az-west-2b traffic. 1% of requests affected but spike in retries.
Carla (sre): ok plan: 1) revert the route-table association to original (rt-0a1) 2) failover NAT to nat-standby in same AZ 3) enable connection tracking sticky fix (short-term). I'm taking lead.
Ben (oncall): handing off to Carla, I'm going to create a postmortem doc stub and update PD notes. (adding reaction :white_check_mark:)
Carla (sre): running `aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-07 --route-table-id rtb-0a1` now.
SRE-Bot: Change detected: route-table-association rtbassoc-07 -> rtb-0a1. Health check: pending.
Carla (sre): verifying return path: `tcpdump -nni eth0 'host 10.0.10.5 and tcp'` shows SYN then RST before NAT translation completes. conntrack table churn high.
Alice (infra): I see a Terraform run from infra-ci user that targeted shared-route-sets and accidentally applied a workspace variable pointing at az-west-2b-subnet mapping. Opening PR to tighten run permissions.
Chris (prod-eng): any customer-facing impact message? we should throttle retries and add graceful fallback.
Carla (sre): short notice: posting status page update - degraded connectivity for a subset of az-west-2b private-subnet workloads. TL;DR: transient route-table swap caused asymmetric return traffic and NAT conn resets; mitigation in progress.
PagerDuty Bot: Escalation: PagerDuty -> On-call Manager (Ben) after 2 pages.
Carla (sre): NAT failover enacted: `aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --vpc-id vpc-0ff` not needed; instead re-associating existing nat-standby nat-67890 to the affected ENIs. traffic normalized for some hosts.
Ben (oncall): I'm updating incident notes with commands run and who approved.
Alice (infra): rolling a quick Terraform rollback to previous route-table config: `terraform apply -var='route_map=stable' -auto-approve`. Running in plan then apply -- watch for drifts.
Carla (sre): monitoring: error rate down from 12% -> 0.9% for affected services. RTT dropped back to baseline. Still seeing a few stale conntrack entries; flushing conntrack on affected NAT instance: `sudo conntrack -F` (performed).
Chris (prod-eng): can we confirm no DNS TTL issues? I saw some timeouts on internal resolver for a minute during the swap.
Alice (infra): internal DNS showed a brief spike in NXDOMAINs due to traffic being NATed incorrectly; resolvers are healthy now, TTLs OK.
Carla (sre): next steps: 1) revert Terraform permission change risk 2) schedule a follow-up postmortem 3) harden route-table change protection (require approval + canary apply) 4) add automated test to detect asymmetric return path via synthetic probes.
Ben (oncall): handing back to infra for long-term, I'll remain available for followups. Oncall handoff note: Ben -> Alice.
Alice (infra): acknowledged. I'll coordinate with Infra-Platform to add safeties. Thanks everyone. (reaction :pray:)
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-0423-1764509876 status => mitigated. Postmortem owner: Alice.
Carla (sre): quick customer impact summary for ops: ~1.2% of inbound requests in az-west-2b (window 16:10-16:46 UTC) experienced connection resets leading to retries. No data loss, only increased latency and 5xxs. Major customers A,B,C saw elevated error rates; support notified.
Ben (oncall): logging final notes and closing incident channel. please add any missing runbook items to the incident doc.
Carla (sre): closing thread, moving conversation to #postmortems for root cause deep-dive.
